reflection.text:
Unblinded truth is vincristine = Tubulin inhibitor / Microtubule destabilizers (e25 PubChem CID 5978, ChEMBL CHEMBL90555, e26, identity check name and BBBC021 structure agree). We concluded Aurora kinase inhibitors p=0.62 (e20) then p=0.48 (e24). Verdict incorrect.

What the evidence actually got right:
The quantitative features and atlas were consistently pointing to destabilizers and were correct. Wells w_099f774aba (0.003 uM, e9), w_f8df549b85 (0.1 uM, e3), w_af047c92af (1 uM, e8), w_5a47dd5361 (10 uM, e2) all showed extreme nuc_solidity z -64.0 to -30.4 and nuc_form_factor z -40.0 to -23.8 with frac_large_nucleus z +16.7 to +20.6, act_std/tub_std z +16.2/+21.4 and cell count drop 483 -> 130 cells. That combination is compatible with potent anti-mitotic microtubule disruption. compare_to_reference_atlas repeatedly returned Microtubule destabilizers 4/10 (e6, e19, e22) with Protein synthesis 5-6/10, and 0/20 neighbors for Aurora - noted explicitly in review critique. Lookup of the atlas top hit demecolcine (e30, CID 220401) is a known destabilizer, and tubulin disruption as a mechanism class is well described PMID 41232862, PMID 27760837, PMID 35803262. The dose-response flags that were statistically null - frac_mitotic_like rho=+0.80 p=0.2 (e12), frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.80 p=0.2 (e11), nuc_dna_integrated rho=+0.80 p=0.2 (e13), cell_count rho=-0.80 p=0.2 (e15) - correctly indicated no robust dose-dependent mitotic arrest or polyploidy increase with n=4 wells.

What misled us and why:
1. Microscopist over-weighting: describe_phenotype on 2 fields repeatedly offered Aurora kinase inhibitors as candidates (e4, also listing Eg5/MT destabilizers; e5 Aurora only; e18 Aurora only; e21 Aurora only on 4 fields but with contradictory density similar vs DMSO). We translated 8-10 observations of lower density and irregular/enlarged nuclei into update_hypotheses Aurora 0.38 (e7) -> 0.65 (e17) -> 0.48 (e23), treating visual grape-like/multilobed micronucleation as Aurora-specific. In reality vinca-site destabilizers produce overlapping large irregular and micronucleated nuclei due to spindle failure, which visual assessment alone cannot resolve without spindle morphology. Our searches for literature to discriminate this returned 0 hits (e28 Aurora vs microtubule, e29 vinca phenotype) and we did not resolve it.

2. Inverted and spurious dose trend misread: e10 nuc_solidity rho=+1.00 p=0 and e14 tub_std rho=+1.00 p=0 were taken as "potent effect" (e17 rationale). The raw values show inversion: most negative solidity at lowest dose (-64.0 at 0.003 uM, e9) and least negative at highest dose (-30.4 at 10 uM, e2). This is the potency inversion flagged in review. With only 4 wells, single rep1 each, p=0 is not credible, and the other trends were non-significant p=0.2. We ignored the contradiction and explained away atlas similarity as "shared cytoskeletal variance without mitotic specificity" (e20).

3. Ignoring the negative atlas and flat mitotic signal: hypotheses e17 and e23 both listed e6/e19/e22 and e12 as contradicting Aurora, yet we kept Aurora as top. Review was explicit: inverted solidity, 0/20 Aurora neighbors, mitotic fraction ~0, all single rep1. We did not act on it. The PI-requested discriminant experiment - describe_phenotype on dose 5 (1 uM) rep1 for tubulin spindle/monopolar vs diffuse (review) - was not acquired as a new well; we reused existing 1 uM fields (e21) which reported diffuse tubulin, no monopolar spindles resolved, and still submitted Aurora 0.48 (e24).

Acquisition choices that caused this:
list_available_experiments showed 8 doses 0.003-10 uM with 4 of 4 wells left (e1) but we sampled only one rep per dose (e2,e3,e8,e9) and never acquired DMSO replicates quantitatively, nor a positive control (e.g. barasertib). All dose_response calculations were 4 wells, 4 doses (e10-e16) - underpowered and vulnerable to selection bias at high dose where cell_count fell to 130. We spent budget on repeated describe_phenotype (e4,e5,e18,e21) and pooled compare_to_reference_atlas instead of replicating the dose-response with n=3 or acquiring high-resolution spindle / phospho-H3 Ser10 readouts we ourselves proposed in e20/e24 next_experiment plans.

Lesson: trust quantitative, replicated atlas voting and dose-dependency statistics (with proper p-values and replicates) over single-rep visual candidate lists, especially when phenotypes overlap. For this compound the correct inference was already in e6/e19/e22 + e25/e26, contradicted by zero Aurora neighbors and flat frac_mitotic_like.
what_was_right: Quantitative irregular nuclei at 3 nM (e9) + tub_std elevation (e2,e14) and atlas Microtubule destabilizers 4/10 in 3 independent comparisons (e6,e19,e22) correctly indicated potent tubulin disruption
Non-significant dose trends for frac_mitotic_like, frac_large_nucleus, cell_count (e11-e13,e15 p=0.2) correctly warned of no clear Aurora-like dose arrest
Unblinding lookup e25/e26 definitively matches vincristine to Tubulin inhibitor
what_was_wrong: Overweighted microscopist Aurora candidates (e4,e5,e18,e21) vs 0/20 atlas Aurora neighbors
Misread inverted nuc_solidity rho=+1.00 (e10) as support when raw z went from -64 (low dose e9) to -30 (high dose e2)
Submitted conclusions e20/e24 without replicates and reused fields for PI-requested discriminant test

mitotic inhibitors disrupting microtubule dynamics produce similar large irregular nuclei phenotypes

reflection.next_experiment: Full replicated dose-response (8 doses 0.001-10 uM, n=3 vs DMSO) + barasertib and vincristine/colchicine positive controls, high-res tubulin spindle imaging to score monopolar vs multipolar/diffuse spindles and micronucleation, plus phospho-H3 Ser10 IF and DNA content to directly test Aurora-B loss vs tubulin-destabilizer mitotic effects; this was proposed in e20/e24 but not executed due to single-rep budget choice.

## Reflection

Unblinded truth is vincristine = Tubulin inhibitor / Microtubule destabilizers (e25 PubChem CID 5978, ChEMBL CHEMBL90555, e26, identity check name and BBBC021 structure agree). We concluded Aurora kinase inhibitors p=0.62 (e20) then p=0.48 (e24). Verdict incorrect.

What the evidence actually got right:
The quantitative features and atlas were consistently pointing to destabilizers and were correct. Wells w_099f774aba (0.003 uM, e9), w_f8df549b85 (0.1 uM, e3), w_af047c92af (1 uM, e8), w_5a47dd5361 (10 uM, e2) all showed extreme nuc_solidity z -64.0 to -30.4 and nuc_form_factor z -40.0 to -23.8 with frac_large_nucleus z +16.7 to +20.6, act_std/tub_std z +16.2/+21.4 and cell count drop 483 -> 130 cells. That combination is compatible with potent anti-mitotic microtubule disruption. compare_to_reference_atlas repeatedly returned Microtubule destabilizers 4/10 (e6, e19, e22) with Protein synthesis 5-6/10, and 0/20 neighbors for Aurora - noted explicitly in review critique. Lookup of the atlas top hit demecolcine (e30, CID 220401) is a known destabilizer, and tubulin disruption as a mechanism class is well described PMID 41232862, PMID 27760837, PMID 35803262. The dose-response flags that were statistically null - frac_mitotic_like rho=+0.80 p=0.2 (e12), frac_large_nucleus rho=-0.80 p=0.2 (e11), nuc_dna_integrated rho=+0.80 p=0.2 (e13), cell_count rho=-0.80 p=0.2 (e15) - correctly indicated no robust dose-dependent mitotic arrest or polyploidy increase with n=4 wells.

What misled us and why:
1. Microscopist over-weighting: describe_phenotype on 2 fields repeatedly offered Aurora kinase inhibitors as candidates (e4, also listing Eg5/MT destabilizers; e5 Aurora only; e18 Aurora only; e21 Aurora only on 4 fields but with contradictory density similar vs DMSO). We translated 8-10 observations of lower density and irregular/enlarged nuclei into update_hypotheses Aurora 0.38 (e7) -> 0.65 (e17) -> 0.48 (e23), treating visual grape-like/multilobed micronucleation as Aurora-specific. In reality vinca-site destabilizers produce overlapping large irregular and micronucleated nuclei due to spindle failure, which visual assessment alone cannot resolve without spindle morphology. Our searches for literature to discriminate this returned 0 hits (e28 Aurora vs microtubule, e29 vinca phenotype) and we did not resolve it.

2. Inverted and spurious dose trend misread: e10 nuc_solidity rho=+1.00 p=0 and e14 tub_std rho=+1.00 p=0 were taken as "potent effect" (e17 rationale). The raw values show inversion: most negative solidity at lowest dose (-64.0 at 0.003 uM, e9) and least negative at highest dose (-30.4 at 10 uM, e2). This is the potency inversion flagged in review. With only 4 wells, single rep1 each, p=0 is not credible, and the other trends were non-significant p=0.2. We ignored the contradiction and explained away atlas similarity as "shared cytoskeletal variance without mitotic specificity" (e20).

3. Ignoring the negative atlas and flat mitotic signal: hypotheses e17 and e23 both listed e6/e19/e22 and e12 as contradicting Aurora, yet we kept Aurora as top. Review was explicit: inverted solidity, 0/20 Aurora neighbors, mitotic fraction ~0, all single rep1. We did not act on it. The PI-requested discriminant experiment - describe_phenotype on dose 5 (1 uM) rep1 for tubulin spindle/monopolar vs diffuse (review) - was not acquired as a new well; we reused existing 1 uM fields (e21) which reported diffuse tubulin, no monopolar spindles resolved, and still submitted Aurora 0.48 (e24).

Acquisition choices that caused this:
list_available_experiments showed 8 doses 0.003-10 uM with 4 of 4 wells left (e1) but we sampled only one rep per dose (e2,e3,e8,e9) and never acquired DMSO replicates quantitatively, nor a positive control (e.g. barasertib). All dose_response calculations were 4 wells, 4 doses (e10-e16) - underpowered and vulnerable to selection bias at high dose where cell_count fell to 130. We spent budget on repeated describe_phenotype (e4,e5,e18,e21) and pooled compare_to_reference_atlas instead of replicating the dose-response with n=3 or acquiring high-resolution spindle / phospho-H3 Ser10 readouts we ourselves proposed in e20/e24 next_experiment plans.

Lesson: trust quantitative, replicated atlas voting and dose-dependency statistics (with proper p-values and replicates) over single-rep visual candidate lists, especially when phenotypes overlap. For this compound the correct inference was already in e6/e19/e22 + e25/e26, contradicted by zero Aurora neighbors and flat frac_mitotic_like.

What was right:
- Quantitative irregular nuclei at 3 nM (e9) + tub_std elevation (e2,e14) and atlas Microtubule destabilizers 4/10 in 3 independent comparisons (e6,e19,e22) correctly indicated potent tubulin disruption
- Non-significant dose trends for frac_mitotic_like, frac_large_nucleus, cell_count (e11-e13,e15 p=0.2) correctly warned of no clear Aurora-like dose arrest
- Unblinding lookup e25/e26 definitively matches vincristine to Tubulin inhibitor

What was wrong or missed:
- Overweighted microscopist Aurora candidates (e4,e5,e18,e21) vs 0/20 atlas Aurora neighbors
- Misread inverted nuc_solidity rho=+1.00 (e10) as support when raw z went from -64 (low dose e9) to -30 (high dose e2)
- Submitted conclusions e20/e24 without replicates and reused fields for PI-requested discriminant test

Proposed next experiment: Full replicated dose-response (8 doses 0.001-10 uM, n=3 vs DMSO) + barasertib and vincristine/colchicine positive controls, high-res tubulin spindle imaging to score monopolar vs multipolar/diffuse spindles and micronucleation, plus phospho-H3 Ser10 IF and DNA content to directly test Aurora-B loss vs tubulin-destabilizer mitotic effects; this was proposed in e20/e24 but not executed due to single-rep budget choice.
